labels.label: theo:geroch
labels.notes: Unmarked; status partial. (1) THE RULED FORM IS DEC-148'S. #check shows geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed has exactly the hypotheses of the printed geroch (unchanged since HEAD), plus [SecondCountableTopology M] and hL : C.LocallyCausallyClosed, with the same TFAE conclusion. Second countability is part of the paper's definition of a topological spacetime (def:category_topological_spacetimes, ETT.tex:255, checked), so it adds nothing beyond the paper. The DEC-148 hypothesis is named a reading (R1: one open U ∋ p with ≤_U closed in U × U). Its (iii)⇒(i) step (geroch_iii_imp_i_of_locallyCausallyClosed) rests on a tagged sorry (l.760), and this is disclosed in the docstring, the SCOPE, REPORT.sorries and REPORT.axioms. The REPORT and the docstrings never call it proved, and they leave its truth open. The R1 reading is a stronger hypothesis than needed (minor finding 1). (2) THE SORRY-FREE FORMS ARE HONEST AND NOT VACUOUS. The engine globallyHyperbolic_of_isCauchySurface_of_isOpen and geroch_iii_imp_i_of_causallyOpen are sorry-free, and so is geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen. The engine adds J^∓(W) open for open W and J^±(S) closed. The repaired forms add CausallyOpen (DEC-8, two-sided) and NonemptyChronalCones. These additions are disclosed: the checklist row is 'strengthened', REPORT.hypotheses[7] and the docstring l.8-9, 41-42. The timelike line satisfies all of them (timelikeLine_engine_hypotheses and timelikeLine_geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen, sorry-free). NonemptyChronalCones excludes BTZ points, and the REPORT says the sorry-free form needs it. (3) ALL FOUR FINDINGS ARE TRUE. [0] holds as qualified in its second sentence, but its first sentence overstates (minor finding 2). [1] holds: a probe checked that chronoMinkowski n (n ≥ 1) satisfies every hypothesis of the engine (chronoMinkowski_engine_hypotheses) and also every hypothesis of geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen except L. The probe used tarentin, cac, SC, J^±(p) ≠ {p} and the measures from chronoMinkowski_counterexample, CausallyOpen from chronoMinkowski_robust, and NonemptyChronalCones from SingularFlatAxioms.mem_Zplus/mem_Zminus_iff with the empty locus. chronoMinkowski has a Cauchy surface, is not locally causally closed and is not globally hyperbolic. Of these facts, only the engine part is a named Lean declaration. chronoMinkowski_not_locallyCausallyClosed is sorry-free: it is derived from the sorry-free SFA form, not from a sorry. [2] holds: under the engine's terms, J⁻(q) ∩ J⁺(S) lies in a compact set (exists_isCompact_Jminus_inter_Jplus), J⁻(q) is closed (the dual of isClosed_Jplus_singleton_of_isCauchySurface) and J⁺(S) is closed by hypothesis, so the set is compact. [3] holds: ETT.tex:255 says 'second countable Hausdorff', and the HEAD form of geroch lacked SecondCountableTopology. (4) The two questions name readings and decide none.

labels.label: theo:geroch_sing
labels.notes: Unmarked; status partial. SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_sing_iii_imp_i_of_locallyCausallyClosed, geroch_sing_of_locallyCausallyClosed, geroch_sing_tfae_locallyCausallyClosed and the two SingularRowsGeroch.*_of_locallyCausallyClosed forms all depend only on the three standard axioms. DEC-149 says the structure carries the closedness 'in charts'. Here it is the hypothesis C.LocallyCausallyClosed on M, beside the frozen strict structure. This is no narrowing: chartwise closedness (each chart domain U_α with ≤_{U_α} closed, or locally closed, in U_α × U_α) gives L on M, because every p lies in some U_α. So the Lean form is at least the chartwise reading, and the REPORT names the reading as its question. ModelMeasures is 'strengthened' for (i)⇒(ii) only. This is pre-existing, as in Causal.SingularGeroch, and disclosed. (iii)⇒(i) takes no measure. 'connected' is dropped, which is a weakening. A probe shows the hypotheses non-vacuous. The SFA form holds on the timelike line: timelikeLine_singularFlatAxioms with timelikeLine_stronglyCausal, timelikeLine_modelMeasures and timelikeLine_locallyCausallyClosed. The E≥0 form holds at E₀: nonvacuous_e0_geroch gives AbsolutelyMinimal, IsoChartsCoverDEC25 and SC, and L follows from GloballyHyperbolic.locallyCausallyClosed with SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms(..).tarentin. Both findings are TRUE. Every input of the engine beyond L is discharged by SingularFlatAxioms (isOpen_Jminus/isOpen_Jplus, sigma_separe_of_isCausal), as the kernel checks. chronoMinkowski with sing = ∅ is excluded by L. The REPORT does not touch CausalScaffold.SingularGeroch.geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal and says so; it is the refuted printed abstraction.

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/GerochEquiv.lean:72-75 (SCOPE), 110-115 (LocallyCausallyClosed), 157-160; REPORT theo:geroch questions[0], hypotheses[5]; REPORT kb_proposals[0]
findings.what: The reading taken for DEC-148 is called 'the weakest of the forms considered', and that is not established. Call R1 the reading taken: one open U ∋ p with ≤_U closed in U × U. Call R2 the listed alternative: ≤_M closed near the diagonal, i.e. each p has an open W with closure(≤_M) ∩ W × W ⊆ ≤_M. R2 is the literal wording of DEC-148 ('≤ closed near every point'). Under the theorem's own hypotheses, strong causality and causal arc-connectedness, the file proves R1 ⇒ R2 (LocallyCausallyClosed.exists_isOpen). The converse is not proved. It does hold under StronglyCausalOpen with cac (take U an open causally convex V ⊆ W; then ≤_V = ≤_M on V), but the theorems carry StronglyCausal (DEC-7, neighbourhoods not open), and that route fails there. So R2 is at least as weak as R1, possibly strictly weaker. In that reading the ruled form geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed may be narrower than DEC-148, and so may the sorry-free engine and repaired forms. Yet the engine uses only R2: every use of hL goes through hloc, ≤_M closed on small compact neighbourhoods, and its time reversal. The REPORT's own question says as much ('which is all the proof uses'). The reading is disclosed and the rows are partial, so this is not a hidden narrowing. Only the characterisation offered to the author is wrong.
findings.fix: State the engine, and with it every repaired and DEC-149 form, with the R2 hypothesis: for each p, an open W ∋ p with closure{≤_M} ∩ W × W ⊆ {≤_M}. Its time reversal is immediate by swap, so the proofs do not change. Keep R1 (LocallyCausallyClosed) as a sufficient condition through exists_isOpen, and (i) ⇒ R2 through isClosed_le (U = M). Then the forms are at least DEC-148 under R1, R2 and the basis reading. Otherwise, at least correct 'the weakest of the forms considered' to 'R1 implies R2 under SC + cac; the converse is shown only under StronglyCausalOpen', in the SCOPE, in question 1 and in kb_proposals[0].

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/GerochEquiv.lean:67-68 (SCOPE) and 760 (the SORRY comment); REPORT theo:geroch sorries[0].obstruction and findings[0] (first sentence)
findings.what: Two wording points. (1) The SCOPE, the SORRY tag and the REPORT say the openness of J^∓(W) 'makes the past-unbounded points and closure J⁺(p) future sets'. The second half is not used. The openness enters only through PastUnboundedAt.of_le (l.626), and through its time reversal inside exists_isCompact_Jminus_inter_Jplus (C := C.dual) (l.670-672, 705-707), where hJp makes the future-unbounded points a past set. exists_frontier_closure_Jplus and the closure argument at l.645-687 use no openness. (2) REPORT theo:geroch findings[0] opens with 'under the repair of DEC-148, (iii)⇒(i) needs no quasi-limit of curves'. That reads as if the ruled step were proved without quasi-limits. It is proved only with the two extra hypotheses, as the finding's next sentence says, and under DEC-148 alone it is open. A finding goes to the author as fact.
findings.fix: (1) Write 'the openness makes the past-unbounded points a future set and, time-reversed, the future-unbounded points a past set' (SCOPE l.67-68, the SORRY comment l.760, REPORT obstruction). (2) Begin findings[0] with 'Under DEC-148 together with J^∓ of open sets open and J^±(S) closed, (iii)⇒(i) needs no quasi-limit …'.

findings.what: The twins are undercounted. The REPORT names two restatements of Causal.Flat.CBGCompact. There are four, each with an identical statement (and, for the first three, an identical proof). PastUnboundedAt (l.196) is PastNoncompactAt (CBGCompact l.91). pastUnboundedAt_of_mem_closure (l.200) is pastNoncompactAt_of_mem_closure (l.95). PastUnboundedAt.of_le (l.207) is PastNoncompactAt.of_le (l.102). exists_mem_frontier_of_le_of_notMem (l.217) is exists_frontier_of_le (l.113). Restating them was right: CBGCompact is model layer, the strict library is frozen, and there is no name clash. But a hoist that removes only the two named would leave two duplicates. CBGCompact's whole `section General` (l.84-405) is model-free and stranded behind a model import (the kb/0047 pattern). The engine's exists_pastUnboundedAt_frontier is its local-closedness sibling, relative to a closed future set A.
findings.fix: List all four twins in the SCOPE and in REPORT notes (6). When the ETT-layer part graduates, hoist CBGCompact's `section General` (or at least the four) into the ETT layer with the same names, and drop the restatements here (kb/0047).

notes: For curation and the loop; these are not defects of the closer. (a) kb/0022 says a printed form believed false becomes a Prop, never a theorem resting on sorry. geroch_iii_imp_i, geroch_tfae_strict and geroch are known false (Causal.not_gerochIIIImpIAsPrinted, not_geroch_tfae; AUDIT-1), yet they stay theorems on an undischargeable sorry, and timelikeLine_geroch_tfae rests on them. The reason is disclosed: SingularGeroch imports geroch, and the curation cites it, both outside this dispatch. The Prop already exists (GerochIIIImpIAsPrinted, CausalScaffold.GerochCauchy). The loop should re-point the theo:geroch row to geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed (ruled, one sorry), with geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen as the sorry-free form, and retire the printed theorems together with SingularGeroch.geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal. The ledger row for theo:geroch still lists Causal.Causality.geroch and geroch_iii_imp_i among its decls. (b) The REPORT's decls mix anchors with refutations and witnesses (chronoMinkowski_*, timelikeLine_*, the printed forms). None of these is an anchor under 'Lean ≥ paper', so map the refutations as findings evidence. (c) The 'every other hypothesis of the sorry-free repaired form' half of finding [1] is true (probe above), but no named declaration carries it. Adding CausallyOpen, NonemptyChronalCones, tarentin, J^±(p) ≠ {p} and the measures as conjuncts to chronoMinkowski_engine_hypotheses would make the finding checkable by name. (d) GerochIIIImpI is a leaf. Add `import CausalScaffold.GerochIIIImpI` to scaffold/CausalScaffold.lean (kb/0025); the joint import was checked clash-free. SingularGeroch's olean is stale but its source typechecks against the new GerochEquiv. (e) The graduation split in REPORT notes (5) is accurate. The sections LocalClosedness and Engine, geroch_iii_imp_i_of_causallyOpen, geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen and the three timelikeLine witnesses are sorry-free and warning-free, and the ETT layer has them. (f) Whether (iii)⇒(i) holds under DEC-148 alone is left open, honestly, with no reading decided. If the fix in finding 1 is adopted, the open question becomes the R2 form, which is at least as strong.
